correctness.rationale: Every quantifier and boundary is explicit: fixed finite T and nu, positive g,k,m,muM,rho,zeta, nonnegative integrable adult-supported basal birth, and \(F(X)/X\) with finite limit. The linearization is block triangular at predator absence. The newborn boundary layer gives \(kL A_\nu(0)/(gJ_\nu(0))\); all older-age terms vanish exponentially and the low-resource limit is zero. The explicit construction satisfies model assumptions and yields \(\mathcal R_F(1)>5643/5000\), small-X limit 0, and high-X limit \(300e^{-10}<1\) for linear birth or zero for saturated birth. Continuity proves at least two threshold roots. Exact inequalities were replayed in the bundled executable; finite quadrature is ancillary. No global nonlinear or transversality conclusion is drawn.

originality.rationale: The main full-text paper supplies the age-renewal model and smooth juvenile/adult weights, and the earlier reproduction-integral analysis supplies the standard fixed-environment invasion test. The present single result derives the previously unstated sharp abundance-asymptotic law for all birth coefficients with \(F(X)/X\) convergent, contrasts the two exact birth forms proposed by the paper, and constructs strict double invasion transitions for both. This is not implied by the published parameter phase diagrams or by fixed-prey monotonicity in g and k. Model-specific conclusions remain narrowly framed; an unindexed broader renewal boundary-layer theorem is an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: A general, uncatalogued boundary-layer renewal theorem might imply the endpoint-limit part, although the joint source-specific original/saturated comparison and explicit double-threshold parameter certificate were not found.

value.rationale: The main ecological mechanism is quantified: increasing prey availability also increases juvenile predator mortality; at very large prey density only a shrinking newborn-age boundary layer survives. Smooth maturation assigns a small but positive birth weight at age zero, making the unsaturated limit finite rather than zero, while the published saturation variant eliminates it. Rigorous double-threshold examples for both alternatives show a meaningful invasion-reversal regime and clarify why choice of maturation smoothing and feeding saturation matters. This is more than a constant-factor calculation or a numerical repeat of the source diagrams.
